title: Difficult & awkward to use; needs strength
text:
Difficult & awkward to use; needs strength. I have a Rosle 8-wedge apple slicer since 2010 and absolutely love it. It is by far the best slicer I ever tried. However, I wanted one that had 16 slices so that I did not have to cut down the 8 wedges in half for when I make cinnamon baked apples. I had a 16-wedge one previously but did not like it and it didn't cut well. Based on my research, this one was recommended. Unfortunately, I'm disappointed. It is just okay.

The slicer has a cover that is attached permanently via a hinge. This makes it awkward to use because that piece is slightly in the way during use. Second, it takes a lot of strength to push this through the apple--even when I put it in my deep sink and press down hard from above. Third, after I flip the cover over to finish pushing this all the way through, when it snaps in place, it still doesn't go all the way through around the entire apple (see my photo where skin and pieces are left behind). I had to be careful and use a knife to remove the debris left behind.

Yes this does make 16 slices, so I'll keep it even though I am not impressed. Had I tried this before buying, I would have never bought it.

The current price of $13.99 plus tax ($14.92 in my case), is competitively priced for this.

description: The Thin Apple Slicer from Prepworks by Progressive is a quick and safe way to easily core and slice an apple. With the Thin Apple Slicer it's as easy as push, flip and pop. Place apple on countertop, stem side down. Simply push the prep works thin apple slicer blades down over the apple, flip the protective cover underneath and pop the apple slices the rest of the way through the blades.
